The kidnappers were incredibly stupid. Their plan was doomed from the get. Go You can't withdraw large sums of money without the bank. They don't just walk into the safe and come out with a big stack of bills. They have to order it most times that's usually a security measure of the bank to not keep large quantities of cash on hand unless you have some sort of high-end private bank. That does such a thing, but even then You're going to have a paper trail.And people noticing paying close attention to a seven million deutsche mark withdrawal. The only hope of any scheme like this working is by using crypto and it being a short exchange. The target is acquired. They are taken out to a remote location. Your identity is completely concealed. No, visible skin, no recognizable voice.
Complete sensory deprivation for the target until absolutely necessary. I mean, extreme lengths, then an immediate crypto transfer will need to take place to a third party of a third party wallet and then it would need to be laundered through multiple different cryptocurrencies. Until eventually, funneled, back to a wallet that you have Of access to but is not under your I. P or email address and the target would have to be abandoned at the remote location told to find his way home or give him a burner. Cell phone with the ability to notify someone you don't want them to perish in the middle of nowhere. And to become a homicide case, you would need to have travel arrangements. Set up to get to flights that have multiple connecting flights in which you made sudden changes to at the moment during the point of transfer as well as once arriving driving. To new countries and paying off the police in these more third world locations under an assumed name to then fly out to your final non extradition location as that new person. The amount of effort that would need to go into this is almost staggering. And for the amount of money that it could render, I just don't see why someone wouldn't take that brain power. I have a real problem with this business model.If aldi is able to not only dictate manufacturer and farmer pricing, as well as speed and schedule of delivery and production.But then, they're also able to increase profits and pricing.Whenever they choose, without those benefits flowing down the pipeline to the producers and manufacturers of the goods.That's a big issue that's not right. Now I'm no socialist, and certainly not a Communist, absolutely not. Those things are evil. However, in the free market, one person in a 2 party or multi-party deal should not be able to dictate the arrangement for everyone. That is not free trade. That is a controlled hostile market. I don't see the point of participating in that. To be honest, it doesn't matter how large the market share is Aldi. Is still Aldi, it's not Kroger or Myers or Walmart. I know many people who don't shop at Aldi. Just because of the reputation, it's considered a poverty store. I used to shop at Aldi. When prices were actually low 10 or 15 years ago, you could go in there and get goods for drastically lower prices than you could anywhere else. And it was worth it now. You might save 10 or 15 cents on an item. Maybe 25 or 50 cents here or there. But the savings don't add up enough to justify leaving your normal market. And since they don't sell brand name goods most of the time, I'm not willing to break brand loyalty for a savings, that's less than 30%. If I have a $300 car to groceries, I want that to be a 2. That said, kidnapping is a really dumb way to make money. In order to really succeed at it, you have to be incredibly sharp.
